note: The Duel's announcer: every moment's lines, 1-3 each, original English with the odd Japanese hype word (hajime, ikuzo, sugoi, kanpeki, yatta, mada mada, sore made). No line quotes or names any other work, character, technique, show or game; the voice is designed, never cloned from or imitating a person or a known announcer. src/audio/duelCaller.ts calls the moments (DUEL_CALLER: priority, chance, rest) and reads the recorded takes from src/audio/data/duelCaller.json by voice and moment; until a voice is recorded, a moment borrows the Rift announcer's fitting line (duelCaller.ts BORROWED) or stays quiet.
archetype: An anime tournament announcer: a big, bright, theatrical voice from the arena's booth, hype that rises with the fight, crisp on the short calls and roaring on the big ones, now and then a Japanese hype word. The voice itself is the one picked of the designed anime-style voices made for the game (which one is set in src/audio/data/duelCaller.json `voice`).
voiceDesign: Designed for the game (never a clone of a person or a known announcer): an energetic tournament caller, clean studio recording, no music, no crowd, no reverb, each line on its own, short (under maxSeconds).
generation: Once a voice is picked: each line by its id, one take each (two for the big moments - round-final, comeback, ko, victory, flawless) in the chosen voice, levelled with the Rift's announcer (the loudest 400 ms at -13 LUFS, as ballCaller.json's are), trimmed, m4a, under public/assets/audio/duel/caller/<voice>/<id>.m4a, and listed in src/audio/data/duelCaller.json by moment. The ball caller's tool (scripts/originals/ball/caller.py) is the model for the preparation.
